parts_missing: sites: usually on scalp, between eyebrows, in nose folds (Skin structure of scalp, Eyebrow structure, Skin structure of nasolabial area all exist)
detail.problem: Red/pink -> Erythema (acceptable; 'Pink skin' finding exists but Erythema covers the intent). Scaly patches -> Scaly skin (acceptable). 'Fine, greasy scales' -> Greasy skin (finding), which in SNOMED is a moistness-of-skin finding (oily skin/seborrhoea), not a quality of the scale; no better concept exists, but it means the nurse must record 'greasy skin' to get the diagnosis, which is a looser match than the page. The distribution (scalp, eyebrows, nose folds, behind ears, axillae, groin, under breasts) is the page's main discriminator from psoriasis and eczema and is not encoded at all, whereas the eczema rule does encode its sites; the resulting rule is effectively 'red + greasy' with no site.
